finding.title: HTTP/1 Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length ambiguity
finding.impact: The old parser could frame a request by Content-Length while ignoring non-exact Transfer-Encoding lists, exposing encoded body bytes as a second request. This is a request-boundary confusion and smuggling primitive when a frontend forwards conflicting framing unchanged; no concrete proxy authorization bypass was demonstrated.
prerequisites: An attacker can submit a request with ambiguous Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length framing.
A frontend or intermediary forwards the conflicting framing to this HTTP/1 backend instead of rejecting or normalizing it.
The frontend and backend disagree about the request boundary in a security-relevant deployment.

implemented_rules: Reject every request containing both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length.
Combine repeated Transfer-Encoding fields in field order before classifying the final coding.
Reject HTTP/1.0 Transfer-Encoding, empty or unknown coding lists, non-final chunked, repeated chunked, and parameterized chunked as invalid framing.
Reject unsupported requests whose valid final transfer coding is chunked with 501 and close the connection rather than falling back to Content-Length or an empty body.
Accept Content-Length only as nonempty ASCII digits after ASCII SP/HTAB trimming; reject signs, non-ASCII whitespace, overflow, and conflicting duplicate values.
Reject comma-joined duplicate Content-Length even when values agree. RFC 9110 permits recipients to reject or normalize that form.
Return a generic mapped 400, 413, or 501 response and close malformed keep-alive connections.
protocol_contract.intentional_limit: Request chunked decoding remains unsupported. Returning 501 without boundary fallback is safe for this implementation but is not complete HTTP/1 request-transfer-coding support.

confirmed_before.result: Parser and real TCP/TLS initial and keep-alive controls dispatched both /outer and an embedded /inside-body request from a gzip, chunked body when conflicting Content-Length was present.

initial_after_compile_failure.result: An accidental removal of the shared header_equals helper broke compilation. The helper was restored; this run is not counted as passing evidence.

coverage: Ambiguous, split, repeated, empty-member, unknown, parameterized, and non-final Transfer-Encoding forms
Initial and keep-alive rejection over real TCP and generated TLS 1.3
Content-Encoding gzip as an opaque Content-Length body followed by a valid pipelined request
Full draining of an ignored body larger than the 64 KiB inline threshold before a legitimate next TCP/TLS request

review_fail_first.result: The final review added a form-feed Content-Length case. httparse rejected the header, but its implementation-specific error text was not mapped to an HTTP status, so the live connection would close without the intended generic 400 response.

final_focused_confirmation.result: All parser and real TCP/TLS framing tests pass after mapping every httparse request rejection to the generic invalid HTTP request class and a 400 close response.

sandbox_only_observation.reason: The restricted sandbox denied loopback bind with EPERM. The same live tests pass outside that sandbox and are included in the final focused and full verification evidence.

independent_gzip_probe.result: Independent gzip decompression reproduced the exact embedded HTTP request used by the live smuggling regression.

pre_review_full_verify.note: No test timeout, retry, framing policy, or performance threshold was relaxed.

full_verify.note: Fresh verification after the final malformed-request mapping passed without a retry or relaxed test, timeout, framing, or performance policy.

test_ideas.disposition: Advisory edge cases were independently checked against source and tests.

broad_review_output_limit.disposition: Incomplete output is retained and not treated as review evidence.

narrow_qwen_review_output_limit.disposition: No review conclusion was accepted from the incomplete response.

narrow_glm_review.disposition: The framing rules were judged sound. Its streamed-body desynchronization concern was checked against the drain implementation and covered by a new real TCP/TLS regression; the initial-version response nuance remains benign but documented.

final_glm_review.disposition: No framing flaw was found. The suggested form-feed Content-Length case failed first, motivated generic httparse request-error mapping, and passes in the final 29-test confirmation. Response Content-Length/remnant handling was independently checked against the shared response writer and focused tests.

methodology.unchanged_inputs: Both measured variants use identical AOT router/client executables, TLS, payloads, driver, timeouts, retries, worker counts, and runtime thread counts. Only the frozen native library changes.
methodology.gbit_definition: Total application request and response bytes divided by lifecycle elapsed; this is not wire bandwidth.
methodology.host: Shared Darwin arm64 host. No audit-owned build, test, or inference workload overlapped timings; unrelated VM and emulator load is recorded in raw process artifacts.

performance.measured_candidate_scope: The successful comparisons use candidate 6ca3966f. The final 1a6d317f binary changes only classification of httparse-rejected malformed requests to a generic 400 response and adds a form-feed regression; valid HTTP request parsing and every measured hot path are byte-for-byte unchanged after the measured candidate.

h1_fresh_short_window.disposition: Retained as an unfavorable short-window signal and investigated with a longer, reverse-order campaign.

ephemeral_port_saturation_attempt.status: stopped on first failure; not rerun
ephemeral_port_saturation_attempt.diagnosis: Back-to-back phases each attempted 8320 fresh connections against a 16384-port range before the expected two-MSL tuple lifetime elapsed. A later reverse-order candidate position succeeds after a 35-second cooldown, excluding candidate-specific connection failure.

controlled_fresh_connection_confirmation.conclusion: The -0.25% throughput delta is much smaller than the roughly 2.4-2.5% within-variant ranges, which overlap. Setup-inclusive operation p50 and p99 are slightly lower for the candidate; mean operation time is 0.30% higher. No material performance regression is reproduced for fresh connections.

final_binary_direct_timing_preflights.status: No timed variant started; both attempts retained and not rerun in place.
final_binary_direct_timing_preflights.disposition: The unchanged quiet-host threshold correctly rejected unrelated local-model inference load. No failed attempt reached a warmup or measured workload, and no external process was stopped. A future distinct campaign may directly time the final binary when the shared host is quiet.

performance.clearance: The affected valid HTTP/1 serial, sustained streaming, and controlled fresh-connection paths show no material throughput, latency, memory, error-counter, or connection-accounting regression from the framing fix measured at candidate 6ca3966f. The final delta is confined to malformed httparse error classification; direct final-binary timing was safely withheld by two busy-host preflights. This is scoped SA-010 valid-path performance clearance, not proof of identical timing or clearance for earlier audit findings.

remaining: Implementing request chunked decoding remains separate compatibility work; safe rejection is covered here.
No named intermediary deployment or end-to-end authorization bypass was reproduced; deployment-specific frontend/backend differential testing remains appropriate.
Malformed later requests receive the connection's initial HTTP version because the failing parser does not expose a trusted later version; the response is generic and the connection closes.
Direct timing of final candidate 1a6d317f remains pending because two frozen quiet-host preflights observed unrelated inference activity and stopped before all timed variants.
Timely delivery from paused long-lived SSE producers is not established by response-completion or request-framing tests.
Earlier security-audit performance findings, finite handle availability, and unreviewed component rows remain open.
